value: Windows Volume Shadow Copy service stopped on a computer that no one told you about
notes: CISA text: the group halts this service to make recovery harder. The service also stops by itself when idle, so a stop alone proves little. Look for it alongside other signs

value: Network storage that holds backups reset to its factory settings
notes: CISA text: the group resets network storage holding victim backups, and in some cases deleted all network-attached backups

value: AnyDesk or TeamViewer installed on a computer by someone other than your IT provider
notes: CISA text: the group installs these legitimate remote tools to move ransomware onto a victim's computers. Many offices use them legitimately, so ask who installed it

value: ScreenConnect that your IT provider did not install
notes: CISA tools table: used by the group for persistence and access. Many IT providers use it legitimately, so ask who installed it

value: VPN or remote access sign-ins from Mullvad VPN addresses
notes: CISA text: the group uses addresses of the VPN provider Mullvad to get initial access, using phished account profiles. Mullvad is a legitimate service used by many people

value: Large uploads to cloud storage with rclone or WinSCP (Mega or Backblaze B2 named) or to OneDrive from a server
notes: CISA text: rclone and WinSCP are used to move stolen data to accounts the group controls, rclone syncing to Mega and b2.exe to Backblaze, and in some cases OneDrive. All are legitimate tools

value: Ransom note on the desktop or in the root folder that points to a chat site on Tor and a victim ID
notes: CISA text: the note says SafePay locked the system and tells the victim to chat over a Tor onion link using a victim ID as the login. Do not visit it
